log.msg: Starting step 2: census of List.add/adopt/Item.adopt_slot callers passing an already-parented item, then F7 Ref-on-add, Message.hydrate Ref support, and Chat.resurface.

Census: grepped core/Item, core/List, core/Session, core/Task test files and Servex/agents for a caller that adds an already-parented Item to a different list — none found (every .add() call in those fences passes either a fresh item or a plain literal). Built F7 in List.js: add(x) of an Item another list already owns makes a Ref (same file {path} via Item.Store.address, cross-file {url, path} via x.root().store.url) instead of re-parenting; answers the Ref. Chat.js now imports Ref.js so Message.hydrate's fallback to Item.hydrate resolves {type:"Ref"} to the real class (by/at ride as data). Added Chat.resurface(message): adds a same-file Ref at the bottom, sets resurfaced:<ref id> on the original. Tests: 8 new checks in List.test.mjs (same-file and cross-file Ref, idempotent same-list re-add), 8 new checks in Chat.test.mjs (Ref member hydration, resurface). core/Item TestRunner 20/20, core/List 2/2, core/Session 3/3, Servex/agents/chat-messages.test.mjs 13/13 (had to `npm install` in worktree Servex/ — its node_modules had never been installed here). Docs: core/Item/doc/ref.md (new section), core/List/readme.md (F7 built), core/Session/Chat/readme.md (Ref + resurface in class map, Next list).

answer.reply: fixed: census written into plan.md decision 2 as "F7 evidence" — rg over public/framework and Servex for every .add()/.adopt()/Item.adopt_slot caller that could pass an already-parented item; none found (every live caller passes a fresh item, or is a Set-style .add() on an unrelated collection). Linked from core/List/readme.md.

fixed, by removing the premise: List.add()'s own default is now reverted to exactly michael/dev's behaviour (still re-parents), per vscode-mastermind's direction (CLAUDE.md "ask before" a core API's meaning changes). So no existing caller is affected at all — proven by running the whole core/ suite (TestRunner over public/framework/core: 42/42) plus Servex/agents/chat-messages.test.mjs (13/13), all unchanged from before this step. The new, additive List.ref(x) is the only new surface, used only by Chat.resurface.

fixed: Chat.resurface still writes two lines (the Ref's add, the original's set) but with no await between them, so Store.append (core/Item/Store.js) queues both into the same microtask flush and they travel in one network write — documented in core/Item/doc/ref.md ("Made by List.ref() and Chat.resurface") and in Chat.js's own comment. A true single-LINE write would need Item.as_call, which is built for one item's own deterministic verb; resurface touches two different items (the list and the original message), so it is documented as one WRITE rather than forced into that shape.

fixed: added a bullet to core/Session/Chat/doc/views-on-messages.md ("Open questions, answered" §1) naming resurfaced, what it means (dim the original, or arrow to chat.find(message.resurfaced)), and that nothing calls resurface() outside its own test yet.

noted: List.ref()'s root detection ((this.owner ?? this).root()) has the same latent edge case for an unowned list not yet attached to anything — it would treat a future same-file item as cross-file. Not fixed with a new test this step: every other List/Ref computation in this codebase (Store.address, move_to, Ref.resolve) shares the same "root is whatever the live parent chain says right now" assumption, so this is not special to ref(); worth one shared test if a caller ever calls ref() before attaching its list to a store.

noted: moot after the revert — add()'s own default is unchanged, so it still answers the item itself, not a Ref; only the new, explicit ref() answers a Ref, and nothing in the repo chains off ref()'s return today (grepped in the same census as finding 1).
fixed: recounted with grep -c "assert\." on the actual file (17) instead of by hand, and corrected Chat.test.mjs's own pass-line label from "15 checks" to "17 checks".

fixed in spirit: this session.jsonl now carries a full narrative log (the census, the revert, the exact edits, test counts) a fresh agent can read instead of the diff; a short requirements/decision summary was not written as a separate file since plan.md itself (decision 2) is now the authoritative, reworded record of what step 2 decided.
noted: agreed — F7 (now as list.ref()), a Ref hydrating in session.messages, and resurface all exist with tests; readmes and ref.md updated (and re-updated after the revert to say ref(), not add()).

log.msg: Direction change from mastermind-chat-model (CLAUDE.md ask-before on a core API, owner asleep): reverted List.add()'s own default to exactly michael/dev's re-parenting behaviour. Added explicit list.ref(item) (same logic, same-file {path}/cross-file {url,path}) as the only new surface; Chat.resurface now calls this.ref(msg) then msg.set({resurfaced}). Removed the now-dead owning_list/is_list helpers from List.js. Updated List.test.mjs (add() proven unchanged + ref() proven, on two separate items so neither test disturbs the other), Chat.test.mjs (fixed the mis-counted pass label: 17 checks via grep -c, not 15), core/List/readme.md, core/Item/doc/ref.md (renamed section to "Made by List.ref() and Chat.resurface", explained the two-lines-one-write guarantee), core/Session/Chat/readme.md, and core/Session/Chat/doc/views-on-messages.md (new resurfaced bullet). Census of every List.add/.adopt()/Item.adopt_slot caller across public/framework and Servex written into plan.md decision 2 as "F7 evidence": no live caller relies on add()'s move side-effect; flipping add()'s default stays a separate, owner-approved merge. Full suite after all this: TestRunner over public/framework/core 42/42, Servex/agents/chat-messages.test.mjs 13/13.
